children: Malaysia's inflation could edge higher to 2.3% in 2027 from an expected 1.9% in 2026, as elevated input and operating costs gradually pass through to consumer prices, Affin Hwang IB analysts Farah Hanini and Vincent Loo say in a note. While targeted subsidies and electricity bill protections will likely continue to contain price pressures this year, inflation is expected to become more persistent, they say. Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to raise the policy rate by 25 bps in 2027, following a pause in 2026, amid firmer domestic demand and broader inflationary pressures, they add. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
